column2: How do I know if there is a new version of LCNDA?
column3: In the desktop app, LCNDA checks on its own at start-up (at most once a day) the latest version published on GitHub. If there is a newer one, a message at the bottom left says so: “⤓ Download”, “See what’s new”, “Later” or “Don’t tell me about this version again”. To check right away: Settings → Help → “🔄 Updates” → “🔍 Check for an update” (or the application menu: LCNDA on Mac, Help on Windows and Linux). Only the question “what is the latest version?” goes to GitHub: nothing from your genealogy, no identifier. To never check: “Check for updates: Never” on the same page. Nothing is shown in Simple mode or in View-only mode.

column2: How do I install a new version?
column3: “⤓ Download” takes the right installer for your computer (Apple or Intel Mac as .dmg, Windows as .exe, Linux as AppImage or .deb depending on what you use), puts it in your “Downloads” folder with a progress bar, then checks its fingerprint (the SHA256SUMS.txt file published with the version): a damaged file is deleted. Then “↗ Open” and you install it yourself (nothing is replaced on its own, the installers are not signed): on Mac, drag LCNDA into “Applications”; on Windows, follow the installation. Your genealogy, media and settings do not move.

Settings → Appearance (“Theme and colours”), at the very top: “🌐 App language”. Eight languages: français, English, Español, Deutsch, Italiano, Português, Polski, Nederlands; the choice is kept straight away on this computer (“↶ Undo” to go back), and can also be made on the first-launch screen. French remains the reference language: the other translations are made by an AI, not by a person. A banner reminds you of this at the bottom right, with “Report a mistake” (it opens “🐞 Report a problem”, already filled in with “translation”); it closes with a click on × and comes back with “Show the banner again”. For now, the app frame is translated (menus, left column, headers, list bar, common windows, dashboard, Settings); records, tools and the FAQ will follow. Your data (names, notes, places) is never translated.

column2: How do I report a problem (a bug)?
column3: Settings → FAQ / tutorial (or About, or “🔄 Updates”) → “🐞 Report a problem”, or the Help menu of the desktop app. Write what happened and what you expected. A technical report is attached, visible and editable: version, system, size of the database in numbers only, useful display settings and the last 50 errors caught. Names, dates, places and file paths are removed from the errors: nothing from your genealogy is in it. Then “📋 Copy”, “Open an issue on GitHub” (the message is ready) or “✉️ Write an e-mail” if an address is set in “🔄 Updates”. Nothing is sent without you.

column2: My database is very big (100,000 people): does the app stay fast?
column3: Yes. It has been tried on a database of 100,000 people (13 generations, 340,000 events, 20,000 places): the list of people, the search (even phonetic), a record, the trees, the map and the lists open in less than a second. Big calculations (statistics, ✅ Database check, GEDCOM export) take a few seconds, with the spinning circle, and the Check is then kept as long as nothing changes. In Lists › Occupations, each occupation shows its first 24 people, then “See the next 24 ↓”. A very large GEDCOM import (100,000 people) takes about a minute.

column2: How do I get back a record deleted by mistake?
column3: Settings → Change log: a deletion is restored with everything that was attached. ⌘Z undoes the last change to a record.

column2: How do I use the spreadsheet?
column3: Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → “🧾 Spreadsheet”, then “＋ New workbook” (or “📋 Start from a template”). Click a cell and type: a number, a text, a record date (“about 1784”, “an II”), or a formula starting with “=” (=SUM(D2:D9)). While typing a formula, click or drag over cells to put them in; the list of functions opens from the first letters (Tab to complete). Sheets are at the bottom (＋, double-click to rename, right-click to duplicate or delete). In the bottom bar: on the left the sheet and the cell (with the sum, average and count of the selection — click to choose what is shown), in the middle some help, on the right the zoom. ↶ ↷ undo and redo everything; “💾 Save” puts the workbook in the list.

column2: How do I enlarge the grid, change the font or set up the spreadsheet?
column3: Zoom: bottom right [− 100 % ▾ +] (⌘+ and ⌘−, ⌘0 to fit the filled columns to the window, ⌘1 for 100 %, or ⌘ + mouse wheel); it is remembered from one time to the next. Font: the “Font” button in the toolbar (or Format → “Aa Font…”) opens the list of fonts of the app and of the computer; the box next to it gives the size (13 px at first); both also go into the Excel file. The column of icons to the left of the grid brings together 🔍 Find, ⚲ Filter, ↕ Sort, ƒ Function, Σ, 👤 Person, 📍 Place, 💬 Note, 📊 Chart, 🎨 Conditional formatting, = Show formulas and ◫ the right panel. “💾 Save ▾” offers a copy, a template or the export. File → “⚙️ Spreadsheet settings…”: each change is kept straight away (“↶ Undo” at the bottom left, “↺ Reset to default”).

column2: What formulas does the spreadsheet understand?
column3: Formulas are written as in Excel in French, with “;” between the parts: SOMME, MOYENNE, NB, NB.SI, SOMME.SI, SI, SI.ERREUR, RECHERCHEV, RECHERCHEX, INDEX, EQUIV, CONCAT, GAUCHE, TEXTE, DATE, ANNEE, DATEDIF, ARRONDI, MEDIANE, UNIQUE, TRIER, FILTRE… English names work too (SUM becomes SOMME). For genealogy: AGE("vers 1784";"an II") → ≈ 10, ANNEE.ACTE("baptisé le 3 frimaire an XII") → 1803, SOSA.GENERATION(12) → 4. “≈” means that a date is approximate. An error (#DIV/0!, #NOM?, #BOUCLE!…) is explained in plain words under the formula bar, with the cell concerned. Insert → “ƒ Function…” shows the whole list.

column2: Do my workbooks keep everything when I exchange them with Excel or LibreOffice?
column3: Yes, for the most part. ⤓ Export → XLSX (Excel) or ODS (LibreOffice) keeps values, formulas (translated into English for Excel), sheets, bold, colours, widths, merges, frozen panes, range names, 💬 notes, validation (choice lists, numbers between two limits), the filter and, in XLSX, conditional formatting. ⤒ Import reads all this back in both directions. Specific to the app: the “👤 person” or “📍 place” cells from the database, record dates in validation, and genealogy functions (AGE, SOSA…), which go out as values. In a formula, Shift + arrows extends the range pointed at (A2 → A2:A4) and brackets forgotten at the end are closed on Enter.

column2: How do I open an Excel, LibreOffice or CSV file in the spreadsheet?
column3: In the spreadsheet: File → “⤒ Import a table…” (or “⤒ Import…” in the list of workbooks). .xlsx (Excel, Numbers), .ods (LibreOffice), .csv, .tsv and .json files are read: several sheets, formulas, bold, colours, widths and merges. For a CSV, the separator and the accents of an old Excel file are guessed. You can also paste a table copied from Excel or Google Sheets (⌘V in the grid). Damaged or booby-trapped files are refused.

column2: How do I export a workbook to Excel, LibreOffice, CSV or PDF?
column3: “⤓ Export ▾” at the top of the spreadsheet: XLSX (Excel, Numbers), ODS (LibreOffice), CSV and TSV (the open sheet), JSON, PDF, 🖨 Print, or the tool’s own file. Formulas go out in English for Excel; those that do not exist elsewhere (AGE, SOSA…) go out with their result. In a CSV, a cell starting with “=” is protected so that no formula can slip in.

column2: How do I sort, filter or clean up a transcription in the spreadsheet?
column3: Data menu: “↕ Sort A → Z” (record dates are sorted by their date), “⚲ Filter” (the search and filter bar of the lists appears above the grid, with “N rows of M”), “Remove duplicates…”, “Split text into columns…” (“MARTIN Jean, 34 ans, laboureur” → 4 columns), “Data validation…” (a choice list, or a person or place from the database chosen with the usual picker, ⌘K). Everything can be undone with “↶ Undo”.

column2: How do I make a chart from the spreadsheet figures?
column3: Choose the range (for example Decade, Men, Women) then “📊 Chart ▾”: the spreadsheet suggests the types that suit the range (decades: the line first; age bands and two series: the pyramid; a single series: the pie chart…) and opens the diagram editor. The diagram stays linked to the range: at the top of its data, “🔗 Data: “Workbook” ! A1:C4 · kept up to date”. Change a figure in the workbook (or add a row just below) and save: the diagram redraws itself wherever it is placed. “Freeze them” cuts the link. The workbook is stored in the Spreadsheet along the way.

column2: How do I edit the figures of a diagram, chart or board in the spreadsheet?
column3: Wherever there are figures, a “🧾 Edit the data” button opens the spreadsheet full size, already set up with the right columns (the blue banner says what is expected): Diagrams (Data tab), Chart editor (“✍️ My own figures”), Presentation (Table and Chart objects), Boards (▦ Spreadsheet object: “🧾 Open in the spreadsheet”) and Collections (one-page spreadsheet). You have formulas, sorting, pasting from Excel… then “✓ Save and go back” sends everything back. A cell like “approx. 12” is counted as 12. The small quick grids remain for 5 rows.

column2: What is “🎯 Prepare for…” in the spreadsheet for?
column3: Data menu → “🎯 Prepare for…”: choose where the data of the range is going (a diagram, a chart, a presentation, a board, a collection). The spreadsheet shows what that place expects and which column it found (✓), flags the cells to check (⚠️ “C7 contains “env. 12”: counted as 12”, with “See the cell”), makes a preview, then creates the thing. For a board or a collection, it copies the range: paste it (⌘V) where you want.

column2: How do I take a Spreadsheet workbook for a diagram?
column3: In the diagram editor, Data tab: “🧾 Take a workbook from the Spreadsheet” (also at the top of “📋 Paste a table”). Choose the workbook with the picker, then the sheet and the range (by default the whole sheet), look at the preview, and choose “Copy once” or “Keep the link” (the diagram then follows the workbook).

column2: I only see 400 rows in the data of a diagram: how do I see the others?
column3: Under the table: “See the next N ↓” adds the following rows (editable like the others, colour included), “See all” adds them all, and “🧾 See all in the spreadsheet” opens everything in the spreadsheet. All rows count in the drawing.
